summary_en: This Phase 3 study tests saruparib added to a hormone pathway drug (ARPI) chosen by the physician, compared with placebo plus that drug, in men with metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer. These men previously had docetaxel or lutetium-177 PSMA therapy and have no disease progression. Saruparib 60 mg is taken by mouth once daily in 28-day cycles, and the ARPI is enzalutamide, darolutamide, or abiraterone, chosen by the physician. The record says the main goal is to measure efficacy compared with placebo, but the specific outcome measure is not stated.
summary_es: Este estudio de fase 3 evalúa saruparib añadido a un medicamento de la vía de las hormonas (ARPI) elegido por el médico, comparado con placebo más ese medicamento, en hombres con cáncer de próstata metastásico sensible a hormonas. Estos hombres recibieron antes docetaxel o terapia con PSMA y lutecio-177, y no tienen progresión de la enfermedad. Saruparib 60 mg se toma por vía oral una vez al día en ciclos de 28 días, y el ARPI es enzalutamida, darolutamida o abiraterona, elegido por el médico. El registro indica que el objetivo principal es medir la eficacia frente a placebo, pero la medida de resultado específica no se indica.
who_for: Men aged 18 or older with metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate adenocarcinoma.
Previously treated with docetaxel or lutetium-177 PSMA therapy, with last dose within 6 months.
No disease progression, with PSA at least 0.2 ng/mL within 14 days before randomization.
Receiving GnRH analogue hormone therapy or has had bilateral orchiectomy.
Tumor tissue and blood sample provided; HRRm, HRD and PTEN status confirmed.
not_for: Prior treatment with a PARP inhibitor or platinum chemotherapy.
ARPI switched earlier for mHSPC because of disease progression.
Severe cytopenia lasting more than 2 weeks, or history of MDS or AML.
Spinal cord compression or brain metastases unless asymptomatic and stable.
Seizure history, or loss of consciousness or TIA within 12 months of enrolment.
